# Cohort 86: exact node target encoding

The five three-level-connect target assertions consume their original selected
event store and the existing closed delivery read owner. The fixed projection
retains exact event, node subscriber type and recipient predicates, without
ordering, limiting, current-state filtering or target reconstruction. PostgreSQL
returns its original JSON/text bytes; SQLite uses its native stored value.

The external assertion still performs the same JSON decode and exact typed
ownership equality, preserving existing/materializing target distinctions.
A finite helper snapshot compares the original SQL and complete decode/assertion
body; the existing whole-caller recipe is updated rather than duplicated.
All five calls have an AST original-owner guard and raw-pool negative.

The unchanged three-level native PG journey runs under race. Separate both-store
controls distinguish two recipients and target kinds, prove two original native
read commits/no writes or active work, and reject foreign event/recipient,
cancellation, closed and absent authority without partial bytes.

This closes only the target observation family. Other nested-connect fixture
raw setup/counters remain counted parent debt. Existing #2542 broad approval
and raw_sql_policy apply; no runtime semantics/spec/framework/tracker changes.
